# Root-block covariance and source occupancy

This supporting note concerns simplices formed from the one-root vertices
of a stochastic retained cone. It supplies exact overlap-safe identities
and upper bounds. It does not assert the proposed mean-cap bridge or any
sharp all-fan score theorem.

Let N=k+r, with k>=1 and r>=1. Let Lambda be an invertible N-by-N
barycentric vertex matrix whose columns have the form

    lambda^l=X_l(h_l,e_(r_l)),
    X_l=1/(1+sum_j(h_l)_j)>0,
    h_l in R_+^k,  r_l in {1,...,r}.                         (1)

This includes every maximum-volume simplex whose vertices come from a
strictly positive stochastic cone with k missed rows and r surviving
roots. Write rho=|det Lambda|. Every root occurs, since otherwise its
row in Lambda would be zero. Let C_s={l:r_l=s}, n_s=|C_s|>=1.

## 1. Exact unweighted root covariance

Define hbar_s=n_s^(-1)sum_(l in C_s)h_l and

    V=sum_s sum_(l in C_s)(h_l-hbar_s)(h_l-hbar_s)^T.

Then

    rho^2=(product_l X_l^2)(product_s n_s) det V.             (2)

To prove this, divide each column by X_l and write the resulting matrix
as [H;C], where C is the root-incidence matrix. Then CC^T=diag(n_s).
The Schur complement of this positive definite block in
[H;C][H;C]^T is exactly V. Taking determinants gives(2).

In particular V must have rank k. Support occurrence alone is
insufficient: the h-vectors must vary in k independent directions WITHIN
their root groups. The trace bound gives

    rho^2<=(product_l X_l^2)(product_s n_s)
                  [sum_s sum_(l in C_s)||h_l-hbar_s||_2^2/k]^k. (3)

If a root occurs only once, changing that column's h_l to zero leaves V
and all n_s unchanged and raises X_l to1. Thus whenever the pure root is
an allowed vertex, a maximum-volume simplex must use the pure root for
each singleton root group. This is strict if its old h_l was nonzero.

## 2. Exact covariance with the normalization retained

The factors X_l can instead remain in the covariance. Put

    s_a=sum_(l in C_a)X_l^2,
    htilde_a=s_a^(-1)sum_(l in C_a)X_l^2 h_l,
    W_*=sum_a sum_(l in C_a)
                 X_l^2(h_l-htilde_a)(h_l-htilde_a)^T.

Then the alternative exact identity is

    rho^2=(product_a s_a) det W_*.                           (4)

This is the Schur complement of the root block of Lambda Lambda^T,
whose root Gram matrix is diag(s_a). It does not discard normalization
loss from large supports.

Let G be any positive definite k-by-k matrix, and choose arbitrary
centers a_s in R^k for each root. Centering at the weighted mean minimizes
the sum of quadratic deviations, so

    tr(G W_*)
       <=sum_l X_l^2(h_l-a_(r_l))^T G(h_l-a_(r_l))=:Q_G.

The eigenvalue arithmetic-geometric mean inequality applied to
G^(1/2)W_*G^(1/2) proves

    rho^2 <= (product_s s_s)/det G * (Q_G/k)^k.               (5)

All group sizes, weights, centers, and repeated support incidences remain
explicit in(4)-(5).

A convenient finite ellipsoid certificate follows. Suppose positive
numbers alpha_s and centers a_s satisfy, for every AVAILABLE retained-
cone vertex X(h,e_s),

    X^2[alpha_s+(h-a_s)^T G(h-a_s)]<=1.                      (6)

Then every source simplex in the cone has capacity at most

    (det G product_s alpha_s)^(-1/2).                        (7)

Indeed the block triangular linear map

    (y,x) -> (G^(1/2)(y-Ax), diag(sqrt(alpha_s))x)

has determinant magnitude sqrt(det G product alpha_s), and(6) bounds
the norm of every transformed vertex by1. The squared norm is convex,
so the bound extends to the polytope. Hadamard proves(7).
This is a valid route for exact rational quadratic certificates; it is
not asserted that a useful certificate always exists for the mean-cap
threshold. Formula(5) can also be used without the uniform bound(6).

## 3. Quantitative nonroot coordinate occupancy

Let mu_j=sum_l Lambda_jl, and let M=sum_(j in missed rows)mu_j.
Every mu_j is positive. Row normalization gives a nonnegative matrix
with row sums1, hence row Euclidean norms at most1. Hadamard yields

    rho<=product_(j=1)^N mu_j
       <=(M/k)^k[(N-M)/r]^r.                                (8)

The second inequality is arithmetic-geometric mean within the two row
blocks. In particular,

    M>=k rho^(1/k)(r/N)^(r/k)>0.                            (9)

The sharper implicit bound in(8) may be used when M<k, because its right
side is strictly increasing on0<M<k. Thus a positive-volume source
cannot put all its coordinate mass in root directions. This occupancy
constraint alone does not control how different sources reuse rows.

Equations(2), (4), and(8) are exact geometric constraints absent from a
relaxation that retains only the largest individual vertex norms. A
proof that they force the desired general mean-cap or sharp fan bound
has not been obtained here.

## 4. Exact ellipsoid certificates for five stress configurations

The file `stress-cone-rational-ellipsoids.json` gives five explicit rational
stochastic matrices of sizes N=6,7,8,9,10 and one indicated surviving-root
set R for each. These are rationalized versions of numerical stress
examples; the assertions here concern the rational matrices in that JSON,
not unspecified numerical approximations. All matrix entries and all
ellipsoid coefficients have denominator10^6.

For each matrix, the JSON also gives a symmetric rational N-by-N matrix Q
such that

    Q is positive definite,
    v(r,A)^T Q v(r,A)<=1 for EVERY retained-cone vertex,
    det Q>4^(N-1).                                         (10)

The exact counts are:

| N | Surviving roots R, one-based | All cone vertices checked |
|---:|---|---:|
| 6 | {5,1} | 32 |
| 7 | {1,5} | 64 |
| 8 | {4,5} | 128 |
| 9 | {2,7} | 256 |
| 10 | {1,5,3} | 384 |

These are general enclosing ellipsoids; they need not have the restricted
block form of(6). Positive definiteness makes the quadratic function
convex, so its bound extends from the listed vertices to their entire
retained polytope. Applying Hadamard to Q^(1/2) times a simplex vertex
matrix gives

    capacity(K_J)<=1/sqrt(det Q)<2^(-(N-1)).                 (11)

Thus each indicated source pattern is impossible for a simplex source
of absolute volume at least2^(-(N-1))V inside an ambient simplex of
volume at most V.

`check_stress_cone_ellipsoids.py` verifies(10) using only exact Fraction
arithmetic: positive pivots of rational symmetric elimination establish
positive definiteness and its exact determinant; the complete vertex
formula checks all864 vertices and their quadratic forms. No numerical
square root, eigensolver, optimizer, or tolerance enters verification.
The report is `audit-stress-cone-rational-ellipsoids.json`.

The proposed mean-cap threshold referred to here is

    [mean_j p_j-|R|/N]/[2^d(Gamma_d-|R|/N)],

under the condition |R|/N<Gamma_d, with d=N-1 and
p_j=product_(l!=j)(1+P_jl)^(-1). For these five matrices it is at least
2^(-d), because mean_j p_j>=Gamma_d. The certified bound(11) therefore
falls below it in these examples. The general proposed bridge is FALSE:
`actual-mean-cap-capacity-bridge-obstruction.md` supplies a different
strictly positive rational matrix and an actual retained simplex above
that threshold. The exact covariance identities and these five finite
certificates do not rely on the false general bridge.


# An actual simplex obstruction to a mean-cap capacity bridge

The following suggested bridge is false, even for a strictly positive
stochastic centroid fan in dimension5:

    capacity(K_J)
      <=[mean_j p_j-r/N]/[2^d(Gamma_d-r/N)],                 (1)

where N=d+1, r=|J^c|, r/N<Gamma_d, and
p_j=product_(l!=j)(1+P_jl)^(-1) are the own vertex-cap fractions.
The example below supplies an actual retained simplex above the proposed
bound. It is not a counterexample to the sharp hitting theorem or
Oertel's conjecture.

Take N=6, d=5, J={1,2,3,4}, R={5,6}, and epsilon=1/10000. Let P have
zero diagonal. In each row j in J, set

    P_j5=1-4epsilon,
    P_jl=epsilon for l not in {j,5}.

In rows5 and6, set every off-diagonal entry equal to1/5. All off-diagonal
entries are strictly positive and every row sums to1. Thus the cuts
lambda_j-(P lambda)_j>=0 form a full positive fan through the uniform
centroid, with the usual strictly positive stationary dependence.

Put

    t=(1-4epsilon)/(2-4epsilon)=2499/4999.

The simplex Q with vertices

    e_5, e_6,
    t e_j+(1-t)e_5, j=1,2,3,4                               (2)

lies in K_J. At the j-th edge vertex its j-th retained constraint is an
equality, because t=P_j5(1-t). Every other retained constraint has left
side zero and nonnegative right side; at the two root vertices those
constraints are strict. The source strictly hits both rows5 and6 at
its corresponding root vertex, so R is its exact hit pattern.
Expansion in the four constrained rows gives

    |Q|/|Delta|=t^4
      =39000037490001/624500149980001.                        (3)

The own-cap fractions are

    p_1=...=p_4
      =1/[(2-4epsilon)(1+epsilon)^4]
      =25000000000000000000/50009998999599964999,
    p_5=p_6=Gamma_5=3125/7776.

Substituting their mean and r/N=1/3 into the right side of(1) gives

    T=156203494652860562789651/2558911628811531009068832.

Direct rational subtraction yields

    |Q|/|Delta|-T
      =449798683564218185227421478115819
         /319672073610396031852077442623411168>0.             (4)

This is an exact geometric contradiction to(1), not a failure of a
particular capacity upper-bound method. It is robust to strict contact
conventions: contract Q by999/1000 about its centroid. All J constraints
then become strict, and its ratio(999/1000)^5 t^4 remains strictly
larger than T. Both claims are exact rational comparisons.

The mechanism is already visible at epsilon=0. The J rows then point
entirely to root5, giving the retained simplex ratio1/16, while those
rows' cap fractions are1/2 and the two root rows' fractions are Gamma_5.
The mean-cap bound becomes Gamma_5/[96(Gamma_5-1/3)], which is less than
1/16 precisely when Gamma_5>2/5; indeed15625>15552 verifies that inequality.
The positive epsilon above removes all zero off-diagonal transitions
while retaining a strict violation.

`check_mean_cap_bridge_obstruction.py` reconstructs the matrix, source
vertices, all retained inequalities and strict hits, the exact volume,
cap fractions, and positive gap using only Fraction arithmetic. It also
verifies the strict-miss contraction. The complete output is
`audit-mean-cap-bridge-obstruction.json`.

The obstruction shows that a uniform average of the row cap fractions
cannot by itself provide the proposed capacity bound. A direction-dependent
weight or another compatibility condition would be necessary for that
approach. No such replacement is asserted here.


# An actual obstruction to stationary-weighted cap averaging

Consider the proposed stationary-weighted bridge

    capacity(K_J)
      <=[sum_j pi_j p_j-pi(R)]/[2^d(Gamma_d-pi(R))],          (1)

under pi(R)<Gamma_d, where pi is the positive stationary distribution of
P and R=J^c. This implication is false for a strictly positive stochastic
centroid fan in dimension5. The counterexample below concerns exactly
that assumption; its uniform hit fraction |R|/N=2/3 exceeds Gamma_5,
so it does not refute a different assertion imposing both conditions.
No Oertel or sharp hitting-center counterexample is asserted.

Let N=6, d=5, J={1,2}, R={3,4,5,6}, epsilon=1/10000, and

    a=(1-3epsilon)/2.

Row1 of P has entries a at columns2 and3, epsilon at columns4,5,6, and
zero on its diagonal. Row2 has entries a at columns1 and3, epsilon at
columns4,5,6, and zero on its diagonal. Each row indexed by R has entries
a at columns1 and2, epsilon at the other three columns in R, and zero
on its diagonal. Thus every row has two entries a and three epsilon,
and all off-diagonal entries are positive.

Every own cap has the SAME fraction

    p=1/[(1+a)^2(1+epsilon)^3]
      =400000000000000000000/900089981998200090009.            (2)

In particular sum pi_j p_j=p. The exact positive stationary distribution
is

    pi=(9997/29997, 9997/29997, 99950012/299999997,
          1/10001, 1/10001, 1/10001).

It sums to1 and satisfies pi P=pi by direct rational multiplication.
Equivalently, the two-state flux between J and R gives

    pi(R)=(1+3epsilon)/(3-3epsilon)=10003/29997<Gamma_5.       (3)

Put t=a/(1+a)=9997/29997. The six vertices

    e_3,e_4,e_5,e_6,
    t e_1+(1-t)e_3,
    t e_2+(1-t)e_3                                           (4)

form a simplex Q in K_J. At its corresponding edge vertex, each retained
constraint is an equality because t=a(1-t). At the other vertices that
row's coordinate is zero and its right side is nonnegative. Each root
row is strictly hit at its own original vertex, so its exact hit set is R.
Expansion in rows1,2 gives

    |Q|/|Delta|=t^2=99940009/899820009.                        (5)

The proposed right side of(1), using(2)-(3), equals

    T=99849982000600210009/1970430673996059729663.

The actual retained simplex exceeds it by

    |Q|/|Delta|-T
      =32126566933877094620869342
         /531963080350738233396309099>0.                     (6)

The violation persists after contracting Q by999/1000 about its centroid,
which makes every missed inequality strict. Thus boundary contacts do
not account for the failure.

The issue is visible as epsilon tends to zero: the three active states
1,2,3 carry equal stationary masses, while the other three surviving
roots have vanishing stationary mass. The retained simplex still uses
all four root directions. Consequently stationary mass alone does not
record their geometric contribution. The example is not a proposal to
replace stationary weights by another fixed mixture.

`check_stationary_cap_bridge_obstruction.py` verifies the stochastic
matrix, stationary distribution, equal cap fractions, actual source
vertices, all cone inequalities, strict hits, exact volume and gap, and
the strict-miss contraction using only Fraction arithmetic. Its full
output is `audit-stationary-cap-bridge-obstruction.json`.


# An exact cyclic-chain finite simplex-source fan

This note constructs a finite simplex-source hitting fan whose24 scores
are all below Gamma_23. It does not, by itself, construct a mixed-integer
body. Any implication through a separate completion theorem must be
independently verified; no such implication is assumed in this proof.

## 1. Ambient simplex and positive fan

Let B be a23-dimensional simplex of volume V/4, with barycentric
coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_23. Indices are taken modulo24. Put

    f_j=lambda_j-lambda_(j+1),
    H_j={x:f_j(x)>=0}, j=0,...,23.                           (1)

All cuts pass through the centroid g_B. Their affine functions sum to
zero, hence their normals have a positive dependence with all24
coefficients equal to1. Their rank is23: if all successive differences
vanish, every barycentric coordinate equals1/24. Thus this is a full
positive fan. Every own cap has exactly half the volume of B, since
exchanging vertices j and j+1 is a volume-preserving affine symmetry of
the simplex interchanging the two sides. Its boundary has23-dimensional
measure zero. Consequently

    |B intersect H_j|=V/8 for every j.                       (2)

## 2. Three actual simplex sources

For a=0,1,2 define the eight-element root set

    R_a={j:j is congruent to a modulo3},

and the retained region

    K_a={x in B:f_j(x)<=0 for every j outside R_a}.           (3)

The constraints split the24 coordinates into eight disjoint chains

    lambda_(r-2)<=lambda_(r-1)<=lambda_r, r in R_a.

For each root r form three barycentric points

    e_r,
    (e_(r-1)+e_r)/2,
    (e_(r-2)+e_(r-1)+e_r)/3.                                (4)

The region K_a is exactly the simplex with these24 vertices. Indeed, a
nonnegative ordered triple (u,v,w) with u<=v<=w decomposes as

    u(1,1,1)+(v-u)(0,1,1)+(w-v)(0,0,1).

Replacing the three unnormalized generators by(4) multiplies their
coefficients by3,2,1 respectively. Summing the resulting coefficients
over all chains gives the total coordinate sum1. This proves convex
containment in the vertices(4); the reverse containment is immediate.
After grouping each chain's rows and columns, the barycentric vertex
matrix has eight3-by-3 blocks of determinant magnitude1/6. Hence

    |K_a|/|B|=6^(-8),
    |K_a|=V/(4*6^8)=V/6718464>V/8388608=2^(-23)V.            (5)

Each source strictly hits every root cut, because f_r(e_r)=1. It misses
all other cuts by(3). Its exact strict hit set is therefore R_a.

## 3. Interior sources and strict missed inequalities

The source centroid g_a has coordinates, along every chain,

    (lambda_(r-2),lambda_(r-1),lambda_r)
       =(2,5,11)/144.                                      (6)

For example, the first coordinate receives1/3 from just one of the24
vertices; the middle receives1/2+1/3; and the root receives1+1/2+1/3.
Define actual smaller simplices

    P_a=(199/200)K_a+(1/200)g_a.                             (7)

All their barycentric coordinates are at least1/14400, so P_a lies in
the interior of B. Every missed f_j is at most-1/9600: its maximum on
K_a is zero, while its centroid value is either-1/48 or-1/24. Every root
support maximum is

    max_(x in P_a)f_r(x)=199/200+(1/200)(1/16)=637/640>0.

Thus strict contacts are not needed for the exact hit pattern R_a.
The sources still meet the required volume threshold. Bernoulli's
inequality gives

    (199/200)^23>=1-23/200=177/200>6561/8192=6^8/2^21.

Combining this with(5) proves

    |P_a|=(199/200)^23 V/(4*6^8)>2^(-23)V.                  (8)

## 4. Exact scores and constant comparison

Assign each of the three sources weight e_a=V/4. The total source weight
is3V/4=V-|B|. Each row belongs to exactly one root set R_a. By(2), its
strict-hitting score is therefore

    |B intersect H_j|+sum_a e_a 1{P_a hits int H_j}
      =V/8+V/4=3V/8.                                      (9)

On the other hand,

    Gamma_23=(23/24)^23>3/8,                               (10)

because

    8*23^23-3*24^23=326771892497780718705079179064>0.

Even the slightly smaller reference M=(999/1000)V satisfies

    Gamma_23 M>3V/8.                                      (11)

Indeed its cross-multiplied positive difference is

    8*999*23^23-3000*24^23
      =159728148498997422430238915779464>0.

Equation(11) is recorded only as an exact margin useful for
checking a separate construction; it is not a mixed-integer inference.

The standard-library checker `check_cyclic_chain_source_fan.py` uses
Fraction arithmetic to calculate all three24-by-24 determinants, all
vertex cuts, centroid coordinates, strict-miss and interior margins,
volumes, exact scores, and(10)-(11). Its full report is
`audit-cyclic-chain-source-fan.json`. No numerical approximation or
optimization is used in the certificate.
